16_marg1403: By a certain prophecy. For Phaleg [is] 'division', because in his days the tongues were divided in Babylon. 16_marg1411: THAMNA. It is asked, since Thamna is read in Genesis to be the concubine of Eliphaz, of the race of the Horrites, who dwelt among the Idumeans in the land of Seir, who bore him Amalec, how she is numbered among the sons, when in what follows that same Thamna is read to be the sister of Lotan the son of Seir, who is also Edom. But Seir in Hebrew means 'hairy', who was rough like a skin; and Edom in Hebrew 'red' or 'tawny'. From this, then, that he sold his birthright for red food, he was called Edom. But the Hebrews solve it thus: they say that Thamna was the concubine of Eliphaz and bore him Amalec, but was brought up by him as a daughter among his sons. Alian, who is of the race of the Horrites, is written Alvan in Genesis, that is, 'exalted'; but in Paralipomenon Alian, that is, signifying 'cast out', because the Horrites were exalted before Edom took their land, but afterwards cast out.

16_marg1447: RABANUS. Four sons of Josias are read here, but at the end of this book and in the book of Kings, where the succession of the kings is, only three are numbered: the first Joathan [so the edition], the second Eliacim, whom Nechao king of Egypt, changing his name, called Joakim, the third Sedecias. Johanan and Sellum are not read there. Whence the Hebrews think that Johanan the firstborn son of Josias was called Joachaz and Sellum. Whence Jeremias: "Thus saith the Lord God to Sellum the son of Josias the king of Juda, who went forth out of this place: He shall return hither no more" etc. For Sellum is interpreted 'carried over'. And as to his saying that Jechonias and Sedecias were born of Joakim: Jechonias is the same as Joachin, who after his father Joakim reigned in Jerusalem three months and ten days. But Joakim, who is also Eliacim, Nabuchodonosor led in chains to Babylon with part of the vessels of the house of the Lord, with whom Ezechiel, still a boy, was carried away, as Josephus testifies; Daniel too and Ananias and Azarias and Misael, as is shown at the beginning of Daniel. Though some affirm that they were carried away with Jechonias the son of Joakim, because Nabuchodonosor carried him too to Babylon with the rest of the vessels of the Lord, and the treasures of the king's house, and the king's mother, and his eunuchs, and the judges of the land, and all the strong men of the army, ten thousand; in whose place was substituted Mathathias, who is also Sedecias, his uncle, the son of Josias, who likewise was carried away to the Chaldeans.

16_interl1811: because our Redeemer stood out above all the height of the saints by the power of his virtue. Whence: "Thou art beautiful above the sons of men" etc., and: "God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows."
16_marg1453: RABANUS. The order seems confused, because, having numbered the sons of Halaa and Naara, he suddenly brings in the kindred of Aharehel the son of Arum, and next tells of Jabes. But the Hebrews say that Assur begot Ethan of Halaa, and he Cos, and Cos Soboba, and Soboba Jabes, who was the teacher of the scribes. Between Cos and Jabes are inserted the kindreds of Aharehel (or Aharahel, otherwise Aral), because he is Obab the son of Aram, that is, Jethro the kinsman of Moses; and because Jabes taught them, they are inserted in his progeny as if born of his forefathers.
16_marg1454: [His mother is] the Synagogue, of which Christ was born, who bore him in sorrow, because she grieved at his coming on account of unbelief. Whence the Jews, envying, said: "If we let him alone so, all will believe in him."
16_marg1455: This fits Christ, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world; of whom it is said: "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world" etc. Him God blessed well with the multiplication of sons, whom holy Church brings forth through the water of baptism. He enlarged his borders, because he gave him the inheritance of all nations and extended his possession to the ends of the earth. With him was the hand of the Lord, because the power of the Godhead did works of power and miracles through him: "He too is the power of God and the wisdom," through whom the Father founded all things that are in heaven and on earth; whom the malice of the Jews could not harm, who says of himself: "The prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing." Through him too are blessed his members, that is, the Church, to whom it is said through Isaias: "Enlarge the place of thy tent" etc. With her is the hand of the Lord, because the Son of God, who is the arm and right hand of the Father, works in her, "and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it," nor shall the devil have dominion over her, because "power is given over all the might of the enemy."
16_marg1456: RABANUS. We read above that Caleb was the son of Hesron, whose brothers were Ram and Jerameel. The Hebrews therefore say that Ram, Caleb's brother, is here called Sua. And Ram is interpreted 'lofty', Sua 'humble', which fits the Jewish people, because it was lofty in the worship of the one God and the power of the kingdom; but because it would not receive the Son of God, it was made humble and vile, that the first may become last.
16_interl1812: namely Bethlehem, or of the mother of Isai, who elsewhere is called Naias
16_marg1457: RABANUS. Some think David is named by the name Recha. For Recha is 'tender'. Whence David says of himself: "I am tender, and anointed king." He too is said to be tender as the little worm of the wood. And they are called the men of Recha because they are noted here to set out the genealogy of David.
16_marg1458: From Saraia Joab is said to have come, who, according to the interpretation of the name, [is] father of the valley of craftsmen, because of his sons were the architects who built the house of the Lord. And the craftsmen who dwell in the valley can be called the teachers of the law, whom "knowledge doth not puff up, but charity edifieth," whom modesty and humility exalt, as Gamaliel and Paul his disciple.
16_marg1459: RABANUS. JEROME. The Hebrews say that Ezra, which is interpreted 'helper', is Amram the father of Moses and Aaron; [that] Jether, that is, 'help', is Aaron; and Mered, which [is] 'rebelling', is Moses; Epher too, or Opher, that is, 'dust', was Eldad, and Jalon Medad, who were two of the seventy elders whom Moses received from God for help in ruling the people. For they hand down that Moses, after receiving the law in the desert, persuaded his father to put away his mother, because she was his aunt, for she was the daughter of Levi; after which Amram married another, from whom he had Eldad and Medad.
16_marg1460: RABANUS. They want Moses to be understood by Sammai, which is interpreted 'heavenly'; Jesba [is] Aaron, which is interpreted 'praise', the father of Esthamo, that is, 'of abiding fire', because the sons of Aaron burnt the sacrifices with fire. And the names that follow in a row are all names of Moses, understood according to his various acts: he is called Jared, that is, 'descending', because he came down from the mountain with the tables of stone; father of Gedor, that is, 'of a hedge', because he surrounded the people with the law as with a hedge; Heber, that is, 'victor', because he joined the people to the service of God; father of Socho, that is, 'of prophecy', because he was the teacher of the prophets; Icuthiel, that is, 'hoping in God', because he had hope of freeing the people from Egypt; father of Zanoe, which is interpreted 'governor', because he governed the people in the desert and governs them daily by his teaching.
16_interl1814: they say this is Jochabed, the mother of Moses and Aaron
16_marg1461: RABANUS. He calls the mother of Moses the daughter of Pharao, who also, according to the proper meaning of the name, is called 'daughter of the Lord', namely because she had a good will in nursing the child; and she is said to have been taken by Mered, that is, Moses, because, leaving idols, she was converted to the worship of God.
16_interl1818: he is set here in memory of the former name of him who was struck by the Lord for his impiety
16_marg1462: RABANUS. He returns to the progeny of Phares, from which David sprang, to finish the progeny of Juda, from which the royal tribe arose, in David. For they hand down that this was Elimelech, the husband of Noemi, in whose time, because of the transgressors of the law, the sun stood still, that, seeing the miracle, they might be converted to the Lord; and because they despised it the famine grew strong, and he who seemed foremost in the tribe of Juda, driven from his country by want with his wife and sons, died with his sons in a strange land.
16_interl1819: who with Beseleel completed the work of the tabernacle
16_interl1820: in the tabernacle of the covenant
16_marg1463: RABANUS. Mahalon and Chelion, who here are called 'secure' and 'going', were in Moab, because they married Moabite wives. Whence in the Hebrew they are called not princes but husbands, as the teachers of that tongue hand down.
16_interl1822: because this history is written in Ruth
16_marg1464: Noemi and Ruth, who returned to Bethlehem, having heard of the abundance of bread.
16_marg1465: By the potters who labour in plantations and hedges we understand the teachers who form and put together the vessels of the Lord; for we say 'fingere', to fashion, for 'componere', to put together; whence we call the fashioners of clay potters. These plant and cultivate the vineyard of the Lord by doctrine, defend it by exhorting and praying. These abide with the king in his works, because, remaining in the faith of Christ, whatever they say, whatever they do, they do for the glory of God.
16_marg1466: The progeny of Ruth, which is said to have dwelt in the hedges and plantations themselves, when this planting came to royal dignity and the defence of the people.
16_interl1823: because from them king David sprang, whose works are extolled with exceeding praises
16_marg1467: In Genesis six are written, but here Sober is passed over, because there is no progeny of him. But certain names are changed for their own reasons. For in Genesis Gemuel, that is, 'sea of God'; here Nabuel, that is, 'reading with God'. One in Genesis is called Echa, here Jarib, that is, 'striving', because from him came Zambri, who, committing fornication with the Madianite woman, was slain by Phinees the priest. Jachim in Genesis, that is, 'preparation', here is named Zara, that is, 'rising'.
16_marg1468: Because Simeon did not have as great offspring as Juda. Whence in Josue it is said that Simeon received his inheritance by his kindreds in the midst of the children of Juda.
16_interl1825: these cities for the most part belong to the tribe of Juda
16_marg1469: Because Siceleg and Bersabee, which were Juda's and had been seized by Simeon, returned under David to the former inheritance of Juda.
16_marg1470: The stock of Simeon and their acts having been described, it is mystically signified that the holy teachers, that is, the princes of the Church, providing pastures for the flocks of Christ, set out into Gador or Gader, which is interpreted 'his hedge'. This is the Church, which is the defence of the faithful; there are pastures as far as the east of the valley, that is, the incarnation of the Word, who "emptied himself, taking the form of a servant." In him are found pastures. For he himself says: "By me, if any man enter in, he shall go in, and go out, and shall find pastures," namely the virtues. In him is a land most broad and quiet, that is, the abundant grace of the Holy Spirit, in which those of the stock of Cham had dwelt before; it signifies that the multitude of the gentiles left idols and flocked to the worship of the one God. These, then, whose names we have written above, came in the days of Ezechias king of Juda, that is, at the coming of Christ. For he is Christ the power of God, whom Ezechias, namely 'strength of the Lord', signifies. They destroyed their tents etc. He strikes by faith the tents of the impious and the inhabitants of the impious when, denying all impiety and worldly desires, he is washed from the filth of sins through the baptism of Christ, afterwards striving to live soberly, justly and piously in this world, that what is written may come to pass: and it shall be in the place where it was said: "You are not my people," there they shall be called the sons of God.
16_marg1471: [They are] the fathers of the new Testament, who went into mount Seir and smote the remnant of the Amalecites, because, trampling on the pride of this world, they crush the deformity of vices. These are said to be four, because, truly instructed by gospel doctrine, they wage spiritual war fittingly against the demons. The remnant of the Amalecites being smitten, they dwelt there, because, the demons being driven out, they put virtues in the place of vices, the possession of which makes a man blessed unto this day; which can always be said until the end of the world, because the Church remains until the end of the world, in which the ancient enemy is daily triumphed over.
16_marg1472: BUT FORASMUCH AS HE DEFILED THE BED etc. The birthright was therefore taken from Ruben, because "he slept with Bala the concubine of his father." And it was given to Joseph, the younger son, whose progeny is multiplied and excels in power of kingdom among the ten tribes. But mystically it signifies the ruin of the former people, which as firstborn ought to have received the priesthood and the kingdom; but because it defiled its father's bed, that is, hung on the cross and killed the body of Christ, in which was "the fulness of the Godhead," the dignity of the firstborn was transferred to the spiritual Joseph, that is, to Christ and the people of the Church, to whom the Father [says]: "Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech."
16_interl1831: Christ, of whom: "The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations"
16_interl1832: because "God hath anointed him with the oil of gladness above" etc.
16_interl1833: the apostles and teachers of the new Testament, of whom it is said: "Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth"
16_interl1834: the dignity of the firstborn and the sovereignty of the kingdom belong to Christ, who is "the firstborn of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth"

16_marg1473: It is likely that Agar was Cethura, since in what follows he says that "the Rubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasses" fought with the Agarens, and that the Itureans, Napheans and Nodab, sons of Ismael, gave them help. And Nodab, it seems, is the one called Cedma in Genesis, that is, 'of the ancients' or 'going before'.
16_interl1839: while the children of Israel served God, they had him propitious and a defender against their enemies; but when, leaving him, they worshipped idols, they felt him an avenger whom they had had as protector
16_interl1840: that is, carried through to the destruction of the enemies by God's help

16_marg1474: AND THE GOD OF ISRAEL STIRRED UP etc. It is to be noted that in Kings it is said that Phul king of the Assyrians received a thousand talents of silver from Manahem the son of Gaddi king of Israel, to be his help and strengthen his kingdom, not that he carried him over to the Assyrians; and that Theglathphalasar king of Assur in the days of Phacee king of Israel took Ahion, and Abel the house of Macha, and Janoe, and Cedes, and Asor, and Galaad, and Galilee, and all the land of Neptalim, and carried them over to the Assyrians. Lastly it relates that Salmanasar king of the Assyrians, besieging Samaria three years, took Osee the son of Ela, king of Israel, and carried Israel over to the Assyrians, and placed them in Hayla and in Abor by the river Goram [so the edition], in the cities of the Medes. Whence it is asked how in Paralipomenon we say that Phul and Theglathphalasar, kings of the Assyrians, carried Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses to Hayla and Abor and Aram and the river Gozan, when Malachim relates that Salmanasar did this, who carried Israel over to the Assyrians and placed them in the aforesaid places. But the former kings of the Assyrians are said to have done this because they began with the Assyrian nation what that same nation completed in their successors. Aram, which Paralipomenon mentions, Malachim passes over. The Hebrews suppose it to be a city [so the edition: 'reges civitatem'] of the Medes.
16_marg1475: The other sons of Levi who likewise were priests in the house of the Lord being passed over, Johanan is especially praised, because he manfully withstood king Ozias when he would sacrifice by himself, and with constancy of mind and zeal for the law fulfilled the office of a priest.
16_marg1476: They say Josedec is Esdras the priest, who, returning from Babylon with Zorobabel and the sons of Juda, restored the temple of the Lord and the city of Jerusalem; which he seems to show in his book when he says: "After these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Azarias, the son of Helchias, the son of Sellum, the son of Sadoc, the son of Achitob, the son of Amarias, the son of Azarias, the son of Maraioth, the son of Zaraias, the son of Ozi, the son of Bocci, the son of Abisue, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron." They also hand down that Esdras is Malachias the prophet, because he also records here many things which are contained in his book, saying: "The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth" etc. Others assert that Josedec is the father of Jesus the high priest, but that Esdras is a priest, a just and glorious man.

16_marg1477: This man, as the Hebrews hand down, when appointed judge took gifts, which Joel, who is also Vasseni, his elder son, knowing it, did not correct. Therefore both are said to have sinned, according to the Hebrews. Whence: "And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he appointed his sons to be judges over Israel" etc.
16_marg1478: By anticipation, while he was telling their genealogy, he touched beforehand on the offices of the singers of David who sang praises to God on musical instruments; but in its own order he will show how they did it.
16_interl1857: by kindred; for Scripture calls near kinsmen brothers
16_marg1479: Ethan [was] one of the three singers who sounded the praise of God on cymbals before David. And it is to be noted that as there were three sons of Levi, Caath, Gerson and Merari, so [there were] three singers: Heman of Caath, Asaph of Gerson, Ethan of Merari. But mystically it signifies the holy teachers who, imbued with the faith of the holy Trinity, according to the dispensation of the true David announce the preaching of the gospel to the whole world.
16_marg1480: THE LEVITES WHO WERE APPOINTED etc. Because every ecclesiastical order, according to the tradition of the apostles, and those who hold the primacy, carry out the whole ministry in the Church of God. Whence: "That thou mayst know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God" etc.
16_marg1481: [Aaron] signifies Christ; his sons, the people of the Church, to whom it is said: "You are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc.; whom the high priest taught to offer upon the altar of faith the holocaust of good works and the incense of prayer, and to pray for Israel, that is, for the state of the Church, according to the precepts of the law given through Moses. And he repeats the genealogy of Aaron as far as Achimaas, which seems to have been done for his praise, because he was faithful to David in all things.
16_interl1868: counting the father, who was the only son of his father
16_marg1482: ALL THESE WERE THE SONS. Wherever it is written in the law, "All these [were] the sons" of this man or that, it is either for the excellence of their merits or for the worsening of their merits, so that they are said to be the sons of him whose imitators they were.
16_interl1870: from whom came forth the Benjamites who by abominable lying with her killed the wife of the Levite
16_interl1874: the concubine of Jacob, the handmaid of Rachel, the mother of Nephtali, from whom these were begotten
16_marg1483: AND HIS CONCUBINE etc. She is said to have been the daughter of a son of Balan, who, brought into Egypt by her father to be sold when famine compelled, was mercifully received in marriage by Manasses, who was over the granaries, food being given to her father.
16_interl1876: who in the Book of Numbers ask of Moses an inheritance among their brethren
16_marg1484: These two names are said to be those of the first son of Machir; but [they say] the second is Salphaat, and their sister Maacha, whom Esrom took to wife when he was sixty years old, who bore him a son Segub, as was said above.
16_marg1485: The sister of Ulam the son of Phares, the son of Machir, as was said before. Some hand down that she was the mother of Jesus the son of Nave, who is called 'goodly man' for the distinction of his virtue and leadership. Others say [she was] Debbora the prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth.
16_marg1486: The Hebrews tell the tale that the sons of Ephraim, gathering a multitude while their father was living, tried to return to the land of promise and were slain in Geth of the Philistines. Hence the other tribes are led through the desert, lest they should see the bones of their brethren; and in the psalm it is said: "The sons of Ephrem turned back in the day of battle."
16_interl1881: the patriarchs who still survived, or kinsmen, who are often called brothers
16_marg1487: WHO WERE REMOVED TO MANAHATH. When for the crime against the wife of the Levite they fell by the sword, and only six hundred remained.
16_marg1488: They were princes, but they submitted themselves to Gera. Hence it is said in the singular: He removed them; from whom came forth the progeny of Gera, who was the father of Semei.
16_interl1899: because they avenged their brethren the sons of Ephraim
16_interl1910: the number refers to the sons of Ulam, so that the sense is: the sons of Ulam were a hundred and fifty, by hyperbaton
16_interl1911: by David, or by Solomon, or by some other king
16_interl1912: partly by Teglatphalasar, partly by Nabuchodonosor
16_marg1489: NATHINEANS. 'Gift', or 'serving in humility'. These are the Gabaonites, whom Josue granted their lives and assigned to the service of the temple, to carry water and wood.
16_marg1490: This was the high priest who found Deuteronomy in the temple of the Lord in the time of Josue [so the edition: 'Iosue'], and he is said to have been the father of Jeremias the prophet.
16_interl1918: who exercised his craft in the house of the Lord and was of the tribe of Levi
16_marg1491: IDITHUN. That is, David's singer. For singers of the sons of Levi kept watch at the king's gate toward the east by their turns, and in turn came together to sing psalms with David; because before the temple was built the ark of the testament was in the palace, and there the keepers served.
16_interl1920: the name of a place, and it is interpreted 'renowned', where Caleb the son of Bara dwelt
16_marg1492: The first Chora is written with aleph and sounds Chora; the second with he, and sounds Chore. Chora is interpreted 'crying out', Chore 'bald'; this is he who in Numbers stirred up sedition against Moses.
16_marg1493: Because they kept the outer door of the tabernacle. But their fathers, who are written below and who have titles in the Psalter, kept the inner door and were singers.
16_marg1494: The grandson of Aaron, who was still living, as the Hebrews hand down, and ordered the courses of the ministers. And there are twenty-four courses, which David ordered for the ministry of the tabernacle. Whence in the gospel: "Zachary, of the course of Abia."
16_marg1495: TO THESE FOUR LEVITES etc. Who these four Levites were, to whom all the number of the porters was committed, is shown when it is said: "And of Hosa, that is, of the sons of Merari, Semri the chief" etc., as is had in the twenty-sixth chapter. The four chiefs of the porters are the holy teachers who, keeping the door of faith by the four gospels, open it to believers and shut it to blasphemers; to whom with Peter the keys of heaven were committed. These keep the doors toward the four winds, because they call the nations to the faith through the four quarters of the world and watchfully keep the Church.
16_interl1922: of the congregation of the Levites
16_marg1496: Mystically, from the company of the holy preachers are ordained those who keep unsleeping watch over the vessels of the Lord, that is, the souls of the faithful, in which the will of God is ministered daily. Under their keeping are the fine flour, wine and oil, with which the sacraments of the body and blood of the Lord are made, and the grace of the Holy Spirit is given by spiritual anointing. They compound in the Church the frankincense of prayers and the spices of virtues, and render acceptable wine in the sight of the Lord.
16_interl1924: with which the ointments and incenses were made
16_interl1925: Christ, "the firstborn of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth"
16_marg1497: Because Christ is the author of the heavenly sacraments, where daily bread and wine are offered in memory of his passion, and [he is] the head of all who after his example crucify their flesh and give it up to suffering for his name.
16_marg1498: They were baked two and two separately before the sabbath, according to Josephus, and on the sabbath morning were set upon the table; of which we spoke more fully in Leviticus.
16_marg1499: It is fitting that the more anyone is set over others, the more devout he should be in the divine offices. He keeps well the chief place of the ministry who is zealous to abide in Jerusalem, that is, in the vision of peace, so as to flee the tumult of the world and the pleasures of the flesh, and to have quiet of mind in the contemplation of God, saying with the psalmist: "I rejoiced at the things that were said to me."
16_marg1500: He who in Kings [is] Abiel, the father of Cis the father of Saul; and it is interpreted 'my father is God'. Jaiel [is] 'forsaken of God', perhaps for the difference of merits. And it is to be noted that among the sons of Jaiel, Cis and Ner are called brothers and are, and so it is had in Kings. But in what follows it is said that Ner begot Cis: not that he begot him, but that he brought him up.
16_interl1929: because neighbours and near kin, though outside
16_marg1501: ABINADAB. This one, who in Kings is related to have been slain with his father, is called Aminadab. And Abinadab is interpreted 'my father [is] a vow'; Aminadab, 'my people [is] a vow'.
16_marg1502: 'Fire [is her] husband'; this is Isboseth, that is, 'man of confusion'.
16_marg1503: 'Striving against the husband'; this is Miphiboseth, which is interpreted 'reproach from the mouth'.
16_marg1504: Many things being omitted which the history in the book of Samuel tells of Samuel and Saul, he records the fall of Saul and his family; mystically hinting that there is no need to describe the life of him whose impious conduct deserved to receive a swift end, and figuratively showing the end of the kingdom of the Jews and of the old priesthood. He has passed over to David, whose deeds and ordering of the kingdom he weaves together, who bears the type of the true David possessing the kingdom of heaven and earth. When he is at hand, the Philistines after their manner fight against Israel and conquer; because as grace drew near the gentiles, as before, assailed the chastity of the Israelite faith, now by showing evil works, now the worship of idolatry, as Balaam taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat and to commit fornication.
16_marg1505: AND THE MEN FLED etc. Those who seemed strong in the contemplation of God, while incautiously they follow the works and teaching of the gentiles. Secular learning also helped not a little toward the perdition of the heretics. Whence someone says: The philosophers, the patriarchs of the heretics, have stained the purity of the Church with perverse doctrine.
16_marg1506: The gentiles rushed in from every side upon the kingdom of Juda and its sons, and corrupted the priests, scribes and Pharisees, that is, its sons and the seducers of that kingdom; the heretics also forbade them to preach or worship simply the grace of the Holy Spirit.
16_marg1507: Lest we should praise with worthy confession the Father who adopted us to himself by a spiritual gift: which the slaying of Abinadab, that is, 'my willing father', signifies.
16_marg1508: Lest we should believe that future salvation is in the kingdom of Christ. For Melchisua is interpreted 'my king [is] salvation'. The philosopher who seduced Arius as it were killed Melchisua; he who [seduced] Macedonius, Jonathan; he who [seduced] Manichaeus, Abinadab; because the master of corruption taught this one to deny the omnipotence of Christ the true king, that one to detract from the gifts of the Holy Spirit, the other to blaspheme the goodness of the supreme Father.
16_interl1941: the gentiles strove with all their strength that the kingdom of Juda should be taken away
16_interl1944: not with swords, that is, by open assault
16_marg1509: AND SAUL SAID TO HIS ARMOURBEARER etc. The Hebrews say this was Doeg the Edomite, who, seeing that Saul was dead, and fearing David, killed himself; but that the young man who brought Saul's diadem and bracelet to David was the son of Doeg, and that Doeg himself was the servant with whom Saul sought his father's asses.
16_marg1510: [The armourbearers are] the teachers of the law. For as the arms and arrows of the Philistines [are] the deceptions of the wicked, so the arms of the Israelites [are] the words of spiritual doctrine, with which the people of God ought to have fortified itself against dangers. Saul, wounded to the point of despair, preferred to perish by the sword of his armourbearer rather than by that of the uncircumcised; because the princes of the Jews, having once taken up the purpose of dying in their sins, preferred to be destroyed by their teachers, who loosed the commandments of the law, rather than be defiled by fellowship with the gentiles. Whence: "They went not into the hall, that they might not be defiled, but that they might eat the pasch."
16_marg1511: BUT HIS ARMOURBEARER WOULD NOT etc. It is not to be doubted that among the reprobate teachers of the law there were some who would not pervert the sharpness of the word to kill their hearers; and yet the hearers themselves, who had received things rightly spoken from their masters, by despising or blaspheming them turned them to their own ruin; and when their death was seen, that is, their obstinacy in sinning, the ministers of the word themselves too, grown worse over time, made the testimonies of the law, which they had feared to interpret wrongly, an occasion of ruin for themselves. Heretics also, bloodied by the darts of their sins, when they drag the divine words into argument for their error, turn their arms against their own breast to their death. Any catholic too, when he defiles the art which he learned for the common good with the contagion of pride, vainglory, love of money or any vice, pierces himself with his own sword, because he has fallen upon that by which he ought to have been defended from the enemy.
16_marg1512: The unlearned, ignorant of the remedies of true humility and of the laver of baptism, seeing their masters in Judea overcome in the spiritual contest, and no small crowd nearest to their hearing put to flight from the ancient seat of its constancy by the pursuing adversary, troubled by the ruin of their elders lost the works of virtues and the defences of spiritual knowledge which they had had; and the sins of the gentiles came and corrupted by perverse indwelling all the pursuits of virtue among the unbelieving Jews. The unclean spirits came and occupied the hearts which constancy of faith had deserted. The nations came and by believing made their own the once excellent pursuits of the Jews. Whence: "The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof."
16_interl1945: that he might reign no more, and to show that the nation of the Jews had lost the kingdom
16_marg1513: The Philistines fastened Saul's head in the temple of Dagon, when the malignant spirits plunge the soul dead in sins into the abyss of hell. For Dagon is interpreted 'fish of sadness'. And he is fitly called a fish of sadness who, plunged into hell, is tormented with eternal pain. So far did the enemies, visible or invisible, pursue Judea with the arms of impiety that they took away the primacy of the kingdom by the root and snatched away the defences of the sacred law. Its overthrow they spread far and wide to their accomplices as a sign of triumph and a cause of joy; and the armour of the heavenly warfare, taken from the Jews, they set equal with their household gods, that is, with the doctrines of demons, either by interpreting spiritual things carnally, or by tossing the divine letters about at will as if they were common. And the nation itself, deprived of the kingdom, as though brought to nothing under the power of its enemies, they set up for a derision and a public byword; which is to have hung up the trunk of Saul's body on the wall of Bethsan, that is, of the house of the enemy, for a show. Heretics also [do the same], when they defraud those laid low by the arrows of sins of the protection of charity, which is the art of the virtues. The unclean spirits as it were cut off Saul's head when they persuade men to follow their own sense rather than that of holy Scripture. They strip him of his arms when they pervert the divine words by a devilish spirit. They put Saul's arms in the temple of Astaroth, which is interpreted 'the making of spies' and signifies the doctrine of the demons who go about seeking whom they may devour, when they change the works by which the faithful had served into the service of their own malice; they hang up the limbs, wholly without light and life, on the wall of the enemy's house.
16_marg1514: First they fastened his head, but afterwards sent it into their land to be carried round for a show. But in Kings it is said that "they hung the body of Saul on the wall of Bethsan"; but the Hebrews hand down that the house of Dagon is called Bethsan, which is interpreted 'house of the sleeper', and that the head and body of Saul were hung there. For the Bethsan in Judges and Josue, which is interpreted 'house of security', is another.
16_marg1515: WHEN THE MEN OF JABES HAD HEARD THIS etc. That is, the men of the Church, remembering that Judea, from which preachers had been sent to them, was mocked by the gentiles, rose up acting manfully, and walking with virtues amid the darkness of the erring, forbade the gentiles to rejoice in mocking her, saying: "If the firstfruit be holy, so is the lump also: and if the root be holy, so are the branches"; "Boast not against the broken branches." The corpses are the carnal, or any carnal things; the bones, the strong, or the works of virtues. They bury the bones in the grove of Jabes when what they find of virtue or firmness in the weak they do not despise as nothing, but join to the fruitful works of the saints: if they know any among the carnal to be zealous for virtues, they number them in the fellowship of the saints. For by the grove the fruit of the good is expressed. But that we read in Kings that the men of Jabes burned the bodies of Saul and his sons signifies that the saints leave the fall of the Jews to the judgment above. Whence: "O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God" etc. According to that: "If anything be left, it shall be burnt."
16_marg1516: [Jabes,] which is interpreted 'dried up', and signifies the Church, which the heat of the sun of justice has dried from every flow of concupiscence. Hence it is described as set on a mountain which is called Galaad, that is, 'heap of testimony', to signify the lofty life of the saints confirmed by fitting testimonies of the Scriptures. This is the city which Saul at the first beginnings of his reign freed from the siege of the enemies.
16_marg1517: AND THEY FASTED SEVEN DAYS. That they might come to rest. For after the six ages of this world, in which we labour in the flesh, follows the seventh, of the rest of souls. Mystically, over the blindness of the Jews who observe the sabbath carnally, their fellow tribesmen, that is, the faithful, grieve continually, and as it were fast seven days. But when the mystery of the eighth day, of the resurrection, has been received, both will rejoice in an everlasting festival.
16_marg1518: But morally, holy men abhor the death of the impious and hand over their examples to the burial of oblivion. They fast seven days, that is, they pass all the time of this life, which turns by the sevenfold number of days, in continence, and abstain from all evil, lest they die in like manner.

16_interl1948: to David: to Christ and the Christian people
