16_marg1520: AND THEY SAID etc. Setting the blind and the lame and the lepers on the walls in contempt of the king, and saying that the blind and the lame forbade him.
16_marg1521: Mystically, David casting the Jebusite out of Jerusalem signifies Christ driving the demons out of the hearts of the faithful and setting his dwelling there. For Jebusite is interpreted 'trodden down', Jerusalem 'vision of peace'. Whence he also says to his disciples: "Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents" etc. Well then is it written in Kings that, the blind and the lame who hated David's soul being cast out, he took the castle of Sion and called it his city; because when Christ drives out of the soul the malignant spirits and the crowd of vices, enlightening it with wisdom, it is rightly called the castle of Sion, that is, of watching, and vision of peace; of which it is rightly said: "In Judea God is known: his name is great in Israel. And his place is in peace."
16_interl1955: because he fortified it with walls
16_marg1522: For he fortified the city by the diligence of a soldier. Yet Josephus says that David fortified the upper city and, joining the castle to it, made one body and surrounded all with a wall; and that he set Joab over the work of the walls, drove out the Jebusites and called it Hierosolyma. For Iero in Hebrew is 'fortification'. Christ too first preached the gospel in Judea and strengthened the Church with the fortification of his faith. Joab, who built the rest of the city, signifies the apostles and apostolic men who after the Lord's ascension converted very many of the gentiles. Whence: "We are God's coadjutors: you are God's husbandry."
16_marg1523: Josephus names him Eusebius, and they say he was the son of Achimee, who, often breaking into the line of the enemy, did not cease until he had slain eight hundred. Others understand him to be David, because Jesbaam is interpreted 'sitting among the people', and Achamoni 'most wise'; whence in Kings it is written: "Sitting in the chair, the wisest." But there he is compared to the little worm of the wood, because his wisdom was lessened on account of the sin which he had committed against Urias. Hence there [he is said] to have slain eight hundred at one onset, but here three hundred; for his fame was lessened by the sin.
16_marg1524: Ahohi, as the Hebrews hand down, was the brother of Isai the father of David, whose son was Eleazar, who was mightiest among the three, whom Josephus says were Eusebius the son of Achimee, and Eleazar the son of Addi, and Semeias the son of Eli.
16_marg1525: GREGORY. Morally. It is to be thought on most earnestly that he who remembers that he has committed unlawful things should strive to abstain even from some lawful ones, so that he who committed what was forbidden may cut off from himself even what is granted, and may reprove himself in the least things who offended in the greatest. The old law forbade coveting another's wife; it does not forbid under penalty that brave deeds be commanded of soldiers by a king, or that water be desired. David, pierced by the sword of concupiscence, took away another's wife, and corrected the evil he had done by the laments of penance; who, when long afterwards he sat against the wedges of the enemy, desired to drink water from their cistern, which chosen soldiers, breaking out among the troops of the enemy, brought unharmed. But, taught by scourges, he at once reproved himself for having desired water at the peril of his soldiers, and poured it out to the Lord, because the water poured out was turned into a sacrifice. For he slew the guilt of concupiscence by the penance of his self-reproof. He therefore who once did not fear to covet another's wife afterwards trembled even because he had desired water. For he who remembered that he had done unlawful things was stern against himself and abstained even from lawful ones.
16_marg1526: BUT YET HE ATTAINED NOT TO THE FIRST THREE etc. Here it appears that Abisai was chief among the three that follow, but did not attain to the first three, Jesbaam, Eleazar and Seminaa. But mystically it is signified that none of the saints, though he excel in virtues, attains to the equality of the power of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: "For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord?" etc.
16_marg1527: That is, lions, as is said in Kings: that is, the strongest men in the kingdom of Moab, as lions.
16_interl1958: which unawares had fallen into a pit full of snow
16_marg1528: The Hebrew judges this lion to be Joab, who was slain in the house of the Lord holding the horns of the altar. For the altar is called a pit [cisterna], because as the water of a cistern cleanses, so the sanctuary of God expiates the sins of men. The Egyptian man whom the book of Kings calls 'worth looking at' [is] Semei the son of Gera, who cursed David, who was of Bahurim, that is, 'of the chosen'. He is called an Egyptian because he imitated the Egyptian blaspheming God whom Moses killed: that one blasphemed God, this one the king and prophet. 'Worth looking at', because he was watched, so that if he went out of Jerusalem he should be killed; having a spear in his hand, that is, the law of God, on which if he had meditated, remaining in Jerusalem, he would not have perished. But because he made the king's command void and went out, Banaias went down with a rod, that is, with the rightness of justice, and wrested from him the spear which he did not hold rightly.
16_marg1529: [Snow,] by which can be signified the grace of Christ which shone upon the world, and the cold of charity with which men grow cold. Banaias, which is interpreted 'the Lord the builder', signifies Christ, of whom it is said: "The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem" etc. He did many works who says: "My Father worketh until now, and I work." He is of Cabseel, that is, of the congregation of the Lord, because the whole company of the saints belongs to him; who, coming down from heaven and made man, slaying by his death the lion, that is, the devil, who possessed the world torpid with the cold of its unbelief, plunged him into hell. He, overcoming by the rod of the cross the Egyptian, that is, Antichrist, blackest with sins, that is, abusing the five senses of the body for crimes, condemned him, guilty by his own wickedness, by everlasting power. In the days of snow, because by his death he expiated sin. Whence: "Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow."
16_marg1530: Abisai and Sobochai and Jonathan, to whom he was equal in strength, who was over the thirty, as the Hebrew affirms.
16_interl1960: as an intimate and faithful counsellor
16_marg1531: THESE ALSO CAME. Up to this point he has enumerated the valiant men of David who helped him to reign over Israel.
16_marg1532: According to the letter it signifies that they were nimble and vigorous in every kind of warfare. But mystically it describes the soldiers of Christ as not sluggish but zealous, in prosperity and in adversity, on the right hand and on the left.
16_marg1533: SWIFT. He says it of sharpness of sense or agility of body. But mystically, those who profess the warfare of Christ ought not to be children in sense, but to provide good things, not only before God but also before all men.
16_interl1985: the teacher of the Church, who is called 'the least' for humility
16_interl1986: of Christ, who are zealous for the virtues of the perfect
16_interl1987: who is strong in knowledge and teaches by word and example, worthy of eternal blessedness, which is designated by the thousand
16_marg1534: This signifies the teachers of the Jews and of the gentiles, of whom Paul, of the tribe of Benjamin, says: "Peter, James and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship" etc. These, coming to Christ, were proved in all things. Whence: "But whom do you say that I am?" Peter answered for all: "Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God." To whom the Lord: "Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church." And elsewhere: "Receive ye the Holy Ghost. Whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them."
16_marg1535: The Jordan, in which Christ was baptized, signifies baptism. This the teachers pass over in the first month, when it is wont to overflow its banks; because when the Lord appeared in the flesh and hallowed the acceptable year, after he had hallowed baptism by his own baptism, they spread it through the whole world by preaching and baptizing.
16_interl1988: unwilling to come to the citadel of the virtues and the summit of wisdom
16_marg1536: AND PUT TO FLIGHT ALL etc. Because by the preaching of the gospel they put to flight the Jews, whom the eastern quarter signifies because of the rising of the knowledge of the law, or the gentiles, in whom natural prudence set, while they ascribe the worship of God to idols. Whence: "Thou hast made my enemies turn their backs upon me, and hast destroyed them that hated me."
16_marg1537: These seven princes, namely, who came from Manasses signify the first teachers of the Church coming from Judea, who, enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit, help our David against the rovers, that is, the heretics or the malignant spirits, who do not cease to snatch from the Church and take captive whom they can. Whence: "Now thanks be to God, who always maketh us to triumph in Christ Jesus."
16_interl1989: sent back by the Philistines as they went against Saul
16_interl1993: who laid waste Siceleg and led away his wives captive
16_marg1538: That is, the one which came out of Egypt, that is, six hundred thousand; so the Hebrews explain it. But mystically, in the army of our David the number of the faithful grows daily, until those are made up who are predestined to eternal life.
16_marg1539: Because the holy teachers most of all desire that the worship of the old law be transferred into the spiritual understanding of the gospel, and that all things be made new.
16_marg1540: The Hebrews hand down that this was Phinees the son of Eleazar, in comparison with whom Sadoc is called a young man, as lesser in age and merit.
16_interl1994: it signifies the number of the priests who were ordained in the house of Sadoc's father, that is, of the Levitical [order]
16_marg1541: AND OF THE CHILDREN OF ISSACHAR. They hand down that there were teachers of the law in the tribe of Issachar, who taught the several times of the ceremonies to be observed and prescribed what Israel should do. These signify the teachers of the Church, whose precepts those under them obey.
16_marg1542: That is, the apostles and apostolic men come together to our David and are joined to him spiritually, and others, both of the Jews and of the gentiles, striving with one heart and equal vow, that David may be made king and they themselves may be the kingdom of Christ.
16_marg1543: That is, holding at all times the faith of the Trinity, and receiving what the first teachers, that is, the apostles, had prepared as food out of divine Scripture, and giving thanks for the bestowal of all good things.
16_marg1544: With the apostles [and] evangelists, who transferred the faith of the incarnation from the Jews to the salvation of the gentiles. For this is to transfer the ark of the Lord to himself from the hill of Cariathiarim, which is in Juda and is interpreted 'city of woods': that is, to lead the faith of the Lord from the height of the Scriptures placed among the Jews, where the woody shade of figures abounds, to the understanding of the gentile people, where the Church is founded.
16_marg1545: Because [unclear in the edition: "interpretatur"] that people could not open the spiritual sense of the old Testament, which lay hid, as it is now revealed to the apostles and prophets: namely, that the gentiles are "fellow heirs and partakers of the promise of the Lord".
16_marg1546: Sihor is a river of Egypt, because, as they say, it is drawn off from the Nile, and it is interpreted 'new and troubled firmament'. Whence: "And now what hast thou to do in the way of Egypt, to drink the troubled water?"
16_marg1547: Cariathiarim [so the edition: 'Chariathiarim']: a city of Damascus, which in Amos [is] Emathabaal, that is, Emath the great, which is now called Epiphania. And by Sihor and Emath he takes in the whole land of promise. By Sihor, that is, the brook or torrent, he signifies the southern part of Egypt; by Emath, the northern.
16_marg1548: Cariathiarim, which elsewhere [is] Cariathbaal, 'city of forests', one of the cities of the Gabaonites in the tribe of Juda, at the ninth milestone from Aelia for those going to Diospolis; of which was Urias the prophet, whom Joachim killed in Jerusalem, according to Jeremias. A son of Sobal is also called Cariathiarim, as is shown above.
16_marg1549: Chosen, [that is,] more noble. And the number of these men is contained in Kings, where we read: "And David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand."
16_interl1998: in Kings Nachon, for which Aquila [has] 'prepared floor'; and Chidon is interpreted 'shield', and is said to be the place where it was said to Josue: "Lift up the shield against the city of Hai"
16_marg1550: They came to the floor of Chidon, that is, 'shield', because in the Church the protection of God is sure. Whence: "O Lord, thou hast crowned us as with a shield of thy good will." Where the priest, touching the ark too incautiously, was struck by the Lord, here also the people of the Jews, which envies the gentiles and, while it would mix the law with the gospel, loses both. The priest being slain, David turned aside the ark of the Lord into the house of Obededom the Gethite; because when the Jews rejected the word of God, the apostles turned to the gentiles. Hence too the place of the floor of Nachon, which shows the preparation of the gentiles, is called the striking of Oza; because, that [people] being left, salvation was made for the gentiles. Obededom, which is interpreted 'serving man', signifies the gentile people, of which it is said: "A people which I knew not hath served me." [unclear in the edition: "Abiecto quoque Iudeorum quasi percussio Oze permittitur sic"]: "Thou wilt deliver me from the contradictions of the people." Geth, which is interpreted 'winepress', signifies the cross, on which the true vine was trodden and pressed. Hence the people of the gentiles can be called Gethite, as though it said: "God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ."
16_marg1551: The Hebrews hand down that Aminadab the priest commanded his sons Oza and Ahio to carry the ark on their shoulders according to the precept of the law. But because they did not carry it, nor give it to the Caathites to be carried, the Lord struck Oza and divided him. For, as they say, his arm withered and [his] shoulders, on which the ark should have been carried, and a distinction was made between obedience and disobedience.
16_marg1552: INTO THE HOUSE OF OBEDEDOM THE GETHITE etc. Because he too was a Levite. And the cause being known for which Oza was struck, David commanded the ark to be carried on the Levites' own shoulders, as appears in what follows. It is to be noted how greatly he offends who receives the body of the Lord unworthily, if a devout priest perished who laid hold of the ark, the figure of the Lord's body, with less veneration than he ought. But allegorically David signifies Christ, the ark the Church, which Christ wills to bring into his city. Whence: "I was not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel." And elsewhere: "Blindness in part has happened in Israel" etc.
16_marg1553: David's many wives signify the many nations which are joined through faith in Christ; the concubines, the churches of the heretics, which glory in the title of the Christian name. But because they follow Christ for carnal gain, they are called not wives but concubines. Now, if kings have several wives it is a crime, because the figures have passed away.
16_interl2000: not out of devotion of faith but by the guile of wickedness; therefore they did not fear to come, because, that is, they would not believe
16_marg1554: When the grace of the gospel was spread abroad and the kingdom of Christ preached everywhere, the nations rose up on every side, gainsaying the gospel of peace.
16_interl2001: showing the gifts of his kindness; but he who was ungrateful got death for himself
16_interl2002: when he joined the faithful to himself by the election of grace and drove out the unbelievers
16_marg1555: IN THE TOPS OF THE PEAR TREES. But in the Hebrew, 'of the weeping ones', that is, of the idols in which they trusted, because they lead to eternal weeping. When, he says, thou shalt hear the sound of one going in the tops of the weeping ones, that is, when thou shalt hear that the idols of the pagans, in which is all their strength, are being destroyed by the angels, then thou shalt go into battle, because the Lord before thee will strike the camp of the Philistines.
16_marg1556: The invisible God, who in his majesty is above all things, shows his presence through invisible things. Whence: "The invisible things of him, from the creation of the world, are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made." It is hinted also to the faithful that they should seek the help of God in all things, and trust that they will prosper in the contest when they feel the coming of the Lord to be with them. And the tops of the pear trees signify the height of the saints. God gives a sign to the holy teachers sent to preach, that they should follow with the ministry of devotion those whom the Holy Spirit directs by warning beforehand.
16_interl2005: of the demons, or the principality of the world
16_marg1557: Christ strikes those who stand on the hill of pride, and breaks the hedge of their hardness, dividing their obstinacy, that he alone may have dominion in the whole world. Whence there follows: And the name of David was renowned etc.
16_interl2008: "He hath given him a name which is above all names"
16_interl2010: the catholic Church spread through the whole world
16_interl2011: because in the present Church he commends the mystery of the incarnation and passion
16_marg1558: THEN DAVID SAID: IT IS UNLAWFUL etc. Christ does not will that the unworthy should discharge the ecclesiastical office, but that men learned in knowledge and approved for uprightness of morals should carry the ark of God, that is, the Church, on the shoulders of devout labour, and exalt it. Whence: "Do the work of an evangelist, fulfil thy ministry."
16_interl2013: the Church, that there, namely, they may venerate the mysteries of the incarnation
16_marg1559: Not only David but also all the prophets in the Church of Christ by words and deeds made room for the incarnation, that, coming, it might be the more quickly received, since it had been prophesied before.
16_marg1560: The ministers of the new Testament ought to be clean in life and doctrine; to whom it is said: "Be ye holy, because I am holy." They ought, by the words of right faith and the example of their work, to commend to the faithful the incarnation of Christ and the redemption of the human race etc.
16_marg1561: Nablum in Hebrew, psalterium in Greek, laudatorium in Latin. The psaltery has a swelling belly in its upper part, so that the strings of the cords, tied on and struck in measured order, may give back a most sweet song. To this the cithara seems contrary, which holds at the bottom what the psaltery holds at the head. The psaltery with ten strings is the Church with the Decalogue of the law. Opposed to it is the cithara, which is made with twenty-four strings in the shape of the letter delta, as the most skilled hand down, and is set going by the fingers in various modes. This signifies the Church, which with the teachings of the twenty-four elders has a threefold form in the shape of the letter delta and signifies the faith of the holy Trinity. And through the hands of the apostles and evangelists it is figuratively set going in the various measures of the old and new Testament, in one way in the letter, in another in the sense.
16_marg1562: The lyre is so called apo tou lirein, that is, from the variety of voices, because it makes different sounds. This signifies the Church, which in the variety of different disciplines, historically, allegorically, tropologically, and by anagoge, gives forth a sweet sound, but does not depart from the simplicity of harmony. And cymbals make a sound when struck against each other. Whence: "Praise him on high sounding cymbals" etc. The well-sounding cymbals are our lips, which, struck against each other, give back the sweet harmony of the human voice.
16_interl2017: on the psaltery they preached the coming of the Saviour, which by a wonderful secret of the Godhead he arranged for the salvation of men
16_interl2018: triumph and palm to God the victor
16_marg1563: FOR THE OCTAVE. That is, they signified the coming of the Lord in the day of judgment, in which, the week of the world being ended, he will come to judgment. Hence the sixth Psalm, which is sung with the trembling of judgment, is headed by such a title. And this number contains great sacraments. Eight souls went into Noe's ark and were saved when the world perished. David, whom the Lord chose, was the eighth son of Jesse. On the eighth day circumcision purifies; on the eighth day, that is, the Lord's day, Christ rose.
16_interl2019: because, full of the spirit of prophecy, he recalled the melodies and words to the memory of the singers
16_marg1564: AND SEBENIAS AND JOSIAS [so the edition: 'Iosias'] etc. These seven priests sounding with trumpets before the ark are the holy preachers, full of the grace of the sevenfold Spirit, who preach the gospel in the Church of Christ and preach the sacrament of the incarnation to their hearers.
16_marg1565: There is one trumpet for gathering the people, another for leading [the march], another for victory, another for pursuing enemies, another for the shutting up of cities, etc. And the customary trumpet, among those skilled in these things, is formed in this way: it is blown into through three brass pipes at a narrow head, so that through four brass voice-channels, which over a brass base put forth four voices, they give out a most mighty bellowing. These signify the gospel, inspired from God by the threefold confession of the three Persons at the narrow head, that is, at the birth of Christ, [sending forth] through four brass voice-channels, that is, through the four evangelists, on a brazen, that is, a steadfast foundation of faith and work, a most mighty voice in the world, as the voice of a trumpet that gathers.
16_interl2020: after "the fulness of the Gentiles shall have come in" to the faith, the ark of God will return into the city of David; that is, it will be turned to the Jews by the grace of Christ, at the preaching of Elias and Enoch
16_interl2023: [unclear in the edition: "triturante"] the ark of God, full of the sevenfold Spirit
16_marg1566: Christ makes manifest the example of his incarnation and passion, before hidden from the Jews. For linen, which springs from the earth and comes by manifold labour to the whiteness of a garment, shows the truth of the human flesh triumphing amid the scourges; and this is: David was clothed with a linen ephod.
16_marg1567: It is pleasing to consider what great gifts of virtues David had received, and how strong he kept himself in humility in all things: [he] whom it did not lift up to break the jaws of lions, to tear apart the arms of bears, to be chosen when his brothers were passed over, to be anointed king when the king was rejected, to lay low the dreadful Goliath with one stone, to bring back the many foreskins proposed by the king when the foreigners had been slain, at length to receive the promised kingdom, to possess all Israel without gainsaying. Yet when he brings back the ark of God to Jerusalem, forgetting that he was set over them, he mingles with the people and dances before the ark. And because to dance before the ark had been, as is believed, the custom of the common people, in the service of God he whirls himself round in a dance. Behold, he whom the Lord preferred to all despises himself under the Lord by making himself equal with the least and showing himself abject. The power of the kingdom is not brought back to mind; he does not fear to grow cheap to his subjects; he does not acknowledge himself as set over others in honour before the ark of him who had given the honour. Before the Lord he did weak or base things, that by that humility he might make firm the man who had done strong things before all. What others think I do not know; I am more amazed at David dancing than fighting. By fighting he subdued the enemy, by dancing himself. And when the daughter of Saul, still mad with the swelling of royal birth, despised him humbled, saying: "How glorious was the king of Israel today, uncovering himself before the handmaids of his servants, and was naked, as if one of the buffoons", she heard: "I will play before the Lord, who chose me rather than thy father", and a little after: "I will play, and I will be made yet more vile than I have been" etc. As if [to say]: I seek to grow vile before men, because I seek to keep the kingdom for myself before the Lord through humility. There are some who think humbly of themselves and, placed in honours, consider that they are nothing but dust, but they shrink from appearing vile to men, and cloak with stiff outward comeliness what they think inwardly. There are some who desire to seem vile to men and wholly despise what they are by showing themselves abject, but inwardly they swell on account of the merit of the vileness they have shown, and are as much lifted up in heart as they press down elation in appearance. Both these wars of elation David detected with great circumspection and overcame with wonderful virtue. For he who, thinking humbly of himself within, does not seek honour without, says: "I will play, and I will be made yet more vile." And because by showing himself vile outwardly he did not swell inwardly, he adds: "And I will be little in my own eyes." As if [to say]: such as I show myself outwardly in despising myself, such I regard myself inwardly.
16_marg1568: While all rejoice and resound with hymns at the entry of the ark, Michol the daughter of Saul alone is absent; nay, from the watchtowers she despises David humbled; because when the Jews believe at the end, some will follow Christ by profession, Antichrist by work. To these it fits that Michol, who is interpreted 'all water' to figure the instability of the carnal, is called not David's wife but Saul's daughter. For those who serve Christ in appearance are not crowned with him, but are condemned with the persecutors whom they imitated. But though the wicked despise the humility of the Church, nonetheless the ark of God comes to its place.
16_marg1569: The ark is set in the midst of the tabernacle which David had pitched for it; that is, the faith of the Church is preached, advances, and is planted in the hearts of the faithful whom God foreordained to eternal life.
16_marg1570: HE BLESSED THE PEOPLE. Christ commends to the Father the faith and devotion of the Church, he who also "at the right hand of the Father intercedeth for us", and as the true David blesses and feeds with the food of the saving mystery.
16_marg1571: These gifts the faithful receive when the many, one bread and one body in Christ, chastising the wantonness of their flesh and bringing it into subjection, bake it in the fire of the Holy Spirit, and make the fruits of good works, made most rich by the oil of mercy, glow with compassion for their neighbour. But on the contrary the daughter of Saul, entering the king's chamber in vain, bears no fruit; because those who receive the word of God with the ear only die without the offspring of good work.
16_interl2025: one, because "one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all" etc.
16_interl2026: "which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life to the world"
16_interl2027: of the fatted calf roasted in the fire of the passion
16_marg1572: Flesh most clean, that is, from the salt of sin, toasted in the frying pan of the cross for the cause of human salvation, full of the oil of charity: "For God so loved the world as to give his only begotten Son", who suffered out of charity.
16_interl2028: showing a clean heart with pure conduct
16_interl2029: meditating on the law of God according to the rule of faith day and night
16_marg1573: IN THAT DAY HE MADE etc. Because Christ set the order of teachers at the summit of ecclesiastical dignity. For Asaph is interpreted 'gathering'. Asaph, then, and his brethren are the apostles and apostolic men appointed to gather the faithful, of whom it is said: "Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth." And the writer of the history inserted the manner of praise which David himself composed, saying: Give ye glory to the Lord etc.
16_marg1574: Alleluia is set as the title of this Psalm, and according to Jerome it is of the neuter gender. Allelu: 'praise ye'; ia signifies the invisible God. It is one of the ten names of God, as Jerome hands down in the letter to Marcella.
16_marg1575: AND LET ALL THE PEOPLE SAY AMEN. That is, the gentile [people], which was still unbelieving when he sang this, yet was brought in by the power of prophecy, that out of love of the whole it should say amen, amen, that is, so be it, so be it; as today amen is answered to the priests when they pray, that the devout intention of the priests and the sound devotion of the people may agree in prayer, according to that: "Amen, amen I say to you, that if two of you shall consent upon earth concerning any thing whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done to them" etc.
16_interl2033: no man, being a soldier to God, entangleth himself with secular businesses
16_marg1576: IN THE HIGH PLACE WHICH WAS IN GABAON etc. Some say that the tabernacle of God, after the children of Israel entered the land of Chanaan, was first in Silo, then in Nobe, afterwards in Gabaon, at last in Sion. Others [say] that a place in Jerusalem was called Gabaon, and that there David set the tabernacle and the ark. For Gabaon is interpreted 'hill'. And they think the place was called high because of the dignity of the divine worship. But in the book of Places we read that Gabaon was the chief city of the Hevites in the tribe of Benjamin. And now a village of the same name is shown at the fourth milestone from Bethlehem toward the west, near Rama and Ramon, where Solomon, having offered victims, merited the divine oracle. And it was set apart for the Levites.
16_marg1577: [unclear in the edition: "Generationi filiorum vacaret"]; others take the blessing by antiphrasis. And the house [is] Michol the daughter of Saul, whom David rebuked because she despised him dancing before the ark of the Lord.
16_marg1578: AND NATHAN SAID etc. It is plain that the spirit of prophecy does not always enlighten the minds of the prophets. Whence Eliseus: "Let her alone, for her soul is in anguish, and the Lord hath hid it from me" etc. Which comes about by divine dispensation, that receiving the Spirit they may find what was of God, and losing it, what was of themselves.
16_marg1579: THOU SHALT NOT BUILD, "because thou art a man of blood." For he who would correct others ought to be clean in himself, so that he flees earthly desires, and sees the more clearly what is to be fled the more truly he himself turns from these by knowledge and life. A hand that holds mud could not wipe away dirt laid upon [another]. This is well said, according to the order of the ancient translation, by a divine voice and by way of signification to David toiling in outward wars: Thou shalt not build me a temple, because "thou art a man of blood." He builds the temple of the Lord who gives himself to correcting the minds of his neighbours. "We are the temple of God", who are established for true life by his dwelling. Whence: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." The man of blood does not build the temple of God. For he who still broods over carnal things must needs be ashamed to instruct the minds of his neighbours.
16_interl2035: he commanded a house of cedar to be built for him by none of the judges, who fought against enemies and were all men of blood
16_interl2036: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses and Josue, whose names [are] famous
16_marg1580: NEITHER SHALL THE CHILDREN OF INIQUITY etc. Foreign enemies [came] at intervals of time, as of old, now peace, now war. Yet there are found there longer times of peace than Solomon had. For under Aod there were eighty years of peace. Far be it, then, that these things be taken of Solomon.
16_marg1581: AND WHEN THOU SHALT HAVE ENDED etc. I WILL RAISE UP THY SEED etc. But Solomon began to reign while his father was reigning, which happened to none of those kings; so that it appears that he is not the one whom this prophecy foreshows. But Christ, the true peacemaker, truly reigned after the death of David.
16_marg1582: AUGUSTINE. He who thinks this promise fulfilled in Solomon errs. He attends to what is said here, He shall build me a house, because Solomon built a noble temple; and he does not attend to what is said, His house shall be faithful etc. Let him attend, then, to Solomon's house full of foreign women worshipping false gods, and the king himself, once wise, seduced into the same idolatry. Nor let him dare to think that God either said or promised this falsely, or did not foreknow that Solomon's house would be such. But in Christ, who was made of the seed of David according to the flesh, we see these things fulfilled; we do not seek another, as the Jews do. For they do not understand this promised son of David to be Solomon, but, he who was promised being made known, they say they hope for another. There went before indeed some image of the thing to come in Solomon, who built the temple and, according to his name, had peace, and at the beginning of his reign was praiseworthy.
16_marg1583: A house, that is, the Church: the house of David because of the race, the house of God because of the temple of God made of men, not of stones, where the people may dwell for ever with God and in God, and God with the people and in the people. Therefore, whereas according to the Septuagint it was said through Nathan: "And the Lord will tell thee that thou shalt build a house for him", afterwards it is said through David: "For thou, O God of Israel, hast revealed to the ear of thy servant, saying: I will build thee a house." For this house both we build by living well, and God by helping. Whence: "Unless the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it."
16_marg1584: It can be taken of the son of Isai by hyperbole. But Christ, who was born of the seed of David, is exalted "above all principality, and power, and virtue", to whom "the Father hath given a name which is above all names, that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow."
16_interl2041: from the power of the devil
16_interl2048: that is, by multiplying his progeny; therefore thou hast given him confidence to speak of thee and to preach thy glory
16_marg1585: The lesser cities belonging to the chief city. For there were five notable cities of the Philistines: Azotus, Gaza, Ascalon, Geth and Accaron. These, because they were in the land of promise and had been assigned to the children of Israel, but had by no means been possessed by them until David, nay, often forced Israel to serve them, David humbled and made tributary. These five cities signify the five senses of the body, because, while the old nature reigns in us, they afflict us with various torments. But when the true David reigns in us they become tributary, and the flesh is forced to serve the spirit.
16_interl2049: but of Christ it is said: "All the kings of the earth shall adore him"
16_interl2050: a city of Syria belonging to the chief city Emath, which is also Epiphania; and that David laid Syria waste Josephus shows
16_marg1586: [Adarezer,] which is interpreted 'comely help', king of Soba, which is interpreted 'kindled' or 'turning', signifies the vices of the gentiles kindled with natural heat, against which Christ fights and conquers "with the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God".
16_marg1587: Christ hamstrings the height of human wisdom that resists him with the pride of the world; yet what he finds fitting and apt for preaching he keeps for himself.
16_marg1588: Damascus, a noble city of Phenice, is interpreted 'cup of blood'; Syria, 'lofty' or 'moist'. For the gentile world, at first fluid with lust and proud in spirit, thirsted for human blood; now, cleansed by the baptism of Christ and exalted by progress in virtues, it longs for the cup of his blood.
16_marg1589: QUIVERS etc. The teachings of the gentiles, in which the liberal disciplines are contained, which Christ took away from the gentile world and turned to the service of the Church; for they are of use for overthrowing error and confirming truth.
16_marg1590: SOLOMON etc. Because, then, our peaceful king turned the old manner of speech, from the humbling of the overthrown gentile world, to the use of the Church, for the cleansing grace of baptism and the strengthening of faith through the preaching of godly doctrine. For Thebath is interpreted 'a little one came', and Chun 'beauty'. For he who knows himself to be little is made fair and comely in the beauty of the virtues.
16_interl2052: Christ sanctifies to the Lord all whom he calls from the gentiles, some distinguished in understanding, others splendid in eloquence, others resounding in preaching, that they may serve faithfully in his tabernacle
16_marg1591: IN THE VALE OF THE SALTPITS. In Kings it is written thus: "And David made himself a name when he returned after taking Syria, in the Vale of the saltpits, eighteen thousand being slain"; because, namely, he set up for himself a triumphal arch. He also made himself a name, because, Syria of Damascus and Syria of Sobal being conquered, he is said to have set up a second.
16_marg1592: But in some copies it is found that David slew not [eighteen but] twenty-eight thousand in the Vale of the saltpits, which came about by the fault of scribes. And Joab laid low twelve thousand, as is written in the title of the fifty-eighth Psalm. But here Abisai is said to have slain eighteen [thousand]; but the victory is ascribed to David for the royal dignity. And because Christ by the strictness of his examination extinguishes, in those who think wrongly of him, the folly of an immoderate taste. Whence: "He that turneth his tongue shall fall into evil."
16_interl2057: 'recorder', that is, they were remembrancers, who brought back to the king's memory the causes noted down
16_interl2059: who in Kings [is] Abimelech, that is, 'my father [is] king'
16_interl2060: who in Kings [is] Saraia; and Susa is interpreted 'joy', Saraia 'prince of the Lord'
16_marg1593: That is, 'my brother [is] king', who in Kings [is] Abimelech, that is, 'my father [is] king'. [The king] of the Church instructs the priests, that those who by the order of dignity hold the place of a father may by humility be reckoned brothers, and may not lord it over the clergy.
16_marg1594: 'Wonderful' or 'life-givers'; whom some say were seventy judges, after the manner of those whom Moses chose in the desert at the Lord's command. Others say that the Cerethites were appointed to punish the guilty, but the Phelethites to defend the innocent.
16_interl2062: in Kings we read, or it is written, that "the sons of David were priests"; but here they are called first and there priests, because of their nobility and precedence
16_marg1595: The sons of David, that is, of Christ, are the faithful whom holy Church bears to him, who are "a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood", first at the king's hand, because by good works they merit for themselves the kingdom of heaven, the nearer to God the holier they are.
16_interl2063: in Kings it is written that "he shaved off one half of their beards, and cut away half of their garments even to the buttocks"; but it is not yet different, because what is lacking here is had there
16_marg1596: HANON, which is interpreted 'their sorrow', signifies the devil, who seems to be ruler of the Ammonites, that is, of the demons, that is, of a people of grief and set in anguish. He shaves half the beard of David's messengers by staining the speech or conduct of the preachers; he cuts their coats as far as the knees or the groin when he reveals in the eyes of men the shameful deeds which he had persuaded. These sit in Jericho until their beards grow, that is, [being] the reproach and shame of others and made accursed by all, until by good endeavour the forms of the beards, that is, of the virtues, grow again, that they may be held worthy of the presence of their king, whose "countenance is against them that do evil things, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth."
16_interl2064: in the Hebrew: when kings had gone forth to war, namely against David
16_marg1597: JOAB GATHERED AN ARMY. Joab began the war, David finished it. For Christ wages war when the order of preachers sets the shield of faith against the powerful of the world; but the end of the contest and the triumph are referred to Christ, who "worketh in us both to will and to accomplish". He fitted to himself the crown which he took from the devil, that is, the faithful, who surround him as a crown. Whence: "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness."
16_marg1598: [He took] the crown and made himself a diadem, because he purified it by melting according to the law. But the Hebrews hand down that, because it was unlawful for a Jew to take any gold or silver from idols, since the law forbids idolatry, Ethai the Hethite, who had come from the Philistines to David, snatched the crown from the head of Melchom, so that it might be lawful for a Jew to take from the hand of a man what it was not lawful [to take] from the head of an idol.
16_interl2065: a city of the kingdom of Ammon which is now called Philadelphia. And Rabbath is interpreted 'many', because "many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven"
16_interl2066: of the idol, which is interpreted 'their king'
16_interl2068: in Kings Gob, that is, 'lake' or 'locust'; and Gazer, 'ordering'; because as locusts [destroy] grass, so the sons of Arapha destroyed the sons of Israel
16_interl2069: in Kings, of the stock of Arapha, because they were the sons of Orpha, the daughter-in-law of Noemi, of the land of Moab
16_marg1599: It is to be noted that in Paralipomenon three wars of David are chiefly read of, in Kings four. For there the fourth war is where, as David was fighting against the Philistines, Jesbibenob, who was of the race of Arapha, the iron of whose spear weighed three hundred ounces, and who was girded with a new sword, attempted to strike David; Abisai the son of Sarvia was a defence to him, and struck and killed the Philistine. But there are also three divisions of times, past, present and future, and four changes [of seasons]: spring, summer, autumn, winter. And the war of Christ is waged at every time of life against enemies visible or invisible in his members, and is triumphed in him. Whence: "Through God we shall do mightily: and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us."
16_marg1600: In the book of Kings thus: "The third was in Gob against the Philistines, in which Adeodatus the son of Saltus, an embroiderer, a Bethlehemite, slew Goliath the Gethite" etc. Gob is interpreted 'lake', because David put himself against Goliath as into a den of lions; who is Adeodatus, that is, chosen for the kingdom. Son of the forest [saltus], namely that in which he fed the sheep; embroiderer, because his mother was of the race of Beseleel; Bethlehemite, because [he was] of Bethlehem, in which Booz was known to Ruth on account of bread; whence the place was called the house of bread. That David himself is Adeodatus is plain where it is said: "These were born of Arapha in Geth, and fell by the hand of David and of his servants." But the Hebrews judge Arapha, the mother of the giants, to be Orpha, the daughter-in-law of Noemi.
16_marg1601: AND ALL THE NUMBER OF ISRAEL WAS FOUND TO BE A THOUSAND THOUSAND. In Kings thus: "That there were found of Israel eight hundred thousand strong men, and of Juda fifty [so the edition: 'quinquaginta'] thousand fighting men." But the Hebrews assert that this number was found by Joab, but that the writer wished to show [unclear in the edition: "nisi quantum"] is written in the books of Samuel, in which only the survivors of the slaughter are contained.
16_interl2070: because of the dignity of the priesthood
16_interl2071: because they had lately fallen almost to extermination
16_marg1602: Death, which first came because of sin [so the edition: 'veni'], raged among the people; because often the life of the shepherd offends for the evil of the flock. David, lifted up with pride, sinned by numbering the people, and the people received the punishment; because the hearts of rulers are disposed according to the deserts of the people. But the just judge, by punishing them, rebuked the fault of the sinner on whose account he sinned. But because, being proud by his own will, he was not free of the fault, he received the punishment of the fault. For the wrath which struck the people in body laid low the ruler with grief of heart.
16_marg1603: In Kings thus: "I have sinned very much in this action. But I pray thee, O Lord, to take away the iniquity of thy servant, because I have done exceeding foolishly." In which it is to be noted that David offended in numbering the people because he did not observe the precepts of the law. For in the book of Numbers the Lord commands Moses: "Take the sum of the children of Israel by their kindreds, whatsoever is of the male sex, from twenty years old and upward" etc. But because David commanded all to be numbered generally, he incurred the indignation of God. In Exodus also the Lord says to Moses: "When thou shalt take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, every one of them shall give a price to the Lord for their souls" etc. Forgetting to do this, David offended God.
16_marg1604: AND DAVID SAID. If he chose famine, he would seem to act against others, because, having much grain, he would not suffer want with the others. If he chose to be overcome by enemies for three months, having most valiant men about him he would fear nothing, while the army would be exposed to slaughter. He therefore chose a suffering common to himself and to others, in which the fear would be equal for all.
16_marg1605: Only the heads of the people and the elders were numbered. But the Hebrews affirm that as many thousands of the whole people were slain as the number written in Paralipomenon exceeds the number which is in Kings. For they say that in Paralipomenon both those who remained and those who were slain were numbered, but in Kings only the living.
16_interl2073: Sadoc the priest, as they say, praying for the people
16_interl2074: of Areuna the Jebusite. For Areuna is interpreted 'threshingfloor', and Ornam sounds in Latin 'light to us'
16_marg1606: Well is David, when he would appease the Lord, commanded to build an altar on the threshingfloor of Areume or Horne; because God is not appeased by man unless on the floor [so the edition: 'arca'] of the heart, by the light of right faith and true love, he set up for him an altar of humility, on which to offer the sacrifice of praise.
16_marg1607: SO DAVID GAVE etc. In Kings thus: "So David bought the floor and the oxen for fifty sicles of silver." Hence the Hebrews suppose that the oxen [were bought] for fifty sicles of silver, but the floor for six hundred [sicles] of gold. But others think that the floor bought for fifty sicles expresses the place of the altar where he offered holocausts, but the floor bought for six hundred sicles is the place of the whole temple which Solomon afterwards built, and its courts.
16_interl2076: under Moses, David, Solomon and Elias fire came down from heaven upon the altar; but under Manue the angel brought forth flame from the rock
16_interl2077: as was commanded in the law; but he had not the time to go there, or perhaps it did not come into his mind
16_interl2078: the stroke of death brought on by the ministry of the angel, as was done in Egypt
